title: Technology Change Management
scenario: Mr. Thompson asks the IT team to formally migrate the school's printer fleet from direct IP printing to a centralized print server with secure release. This change affects every faculty and staff member. The change must be planned, reviewed by the Change Advisory Board, and rolled out during the next break week.
impact: Strategic: a poorly planned change will disrupt printing for the entire school. The CAB process is mandatory for any change affecting more than 25 users. A failed change erodes trust in IT.
objectives: Draft a formal change request following the school CAB template
Identify the scope, risk, and rollback plan for the change
Schedule the CAB review and present the change for approval
Communicate the change window and impact to all affected users
Execute the change during the approved maintenance window
Validate the change and document the outcome in the change log

evidence.description: Completed change request with scope, risk, rollback, and approver list
CAB meeting minutes recording the approval decision and conditions
Post-change validation report and user communication

decisionPoints.prompt: The change affects 180 faculty and staff users. What is the correct change classification?

options.label: Standard change — skip CAB review because the change is well understood
options.feedback: A change affecting 180 users with a network-wide service is not standard. It must go through CAB review.

options.label: Normal change — full CAB review with risk assessment, rollback, and approval required
options.feedback: Correct — a fleet-wide print server migration is a normal change. CAB review is mandatory for transparency and risk control.

options.label: Emergency change — fast-track with no review because it improves security
options.feedback: Emergency change classification is for unplanned outages only, not planned improvements. Fast-tracking planned changes violates process.

decisionPoints.prompt: Mid-rollout, 12 users report they cannot release print jobs. What is the correct response?

options.label: Continue the rollout to all 180 users and address issues afterwards
options.feedback: Continuing a rollout with known issues breaks your risk plan and may impact all 180 users before the cause is known.

options.label: Pause the rollout, investigate the issue, and decide whether to proceed or invoke the rollback plan
options.feedback: Correct — pause, investigate, then decide. The pre-approved rollback plan is the safety net, not a sign of failure.

options.label: Invoke the full rollback immediately and cancel the change
options.feedback: Full rollback may be premature. Investigate first to determine whether the issue is widespread or limited to a known cause.

ticket.initialDescription: Mr. Thompson requests a change to migrate the printer fleet from direct IP printing to a centralized print server with secure release. Affects 180 users. Maintenance window: next break week.

state.title: Printer fleet migration to print server with secure release
state.rollback_plan: revert to direct IP, restore prior printer objects

nodes.title: Scope the change
nodes.body: Review the change request from Mr. Thompson. Confirm the scope (180 users, 24 printers), the maintenance window, and the CAB approval requirements. Identify all stakeholders.

nodes.title: Draft the change request
nodes.body: Complete the CAB change request template: scope, risk assessment, rollback plan, communication plan, validation plan, and approver list. Save the draft as evidence.

nodes.title: Classify the change
nodes.body: Choose the correct change classification for a 180-user fleet-wide print server migration.

nodes.title: Present at CAB
nodes.body: Present the change to the CAB. Capture the decision, any conditions, and the approvers. Save the CAB minutes as evidence.

nodes.title: Execute the change in the maintenance window
nodes.body: During the approved window, deploy the print server, migrate printer objects in batches, and update user devices. Monitor for errors. If issues exceed threshold, pause and decide next step.

nodes.title: Decide on rollback
nodes.body: 12 users report a release failure mid-rollout. Choose the correct response.

nodes.title: Validate post-change
nodes.body: Run the post-change validation: print from each user class (faculty, staff, admin), confirm secure release works, check the print server load. Save the validation report as evidence.

nodes.title: Close the change
nodes.body: Update the change log with the outcome, lessons learned, and any follow-up actions. Communicate the change completion to faculty and staff.
nodes.prompt: Write the post-change communication to faculty and staff: what changed, what they need to do, and how to get help if printing does not work.

nodes.title: Debrief
nodes.body: Review the change process. Key lessons: every fleet-wide change goes through CAB, always have a documented rollback plan, and a paused rollout is not a failure — it is risk control working.

kbOpportunity: Change management workflow: draft change → classify (standard / normal / emergency) → CAB review → risk + rollback plan → approved window execution → validation → change log closeout.
